Statutory Protection Suite IT Act Sec 79 & DPDPA 2023

Statutory Compliance, Intermediary Immunity & Law Enforcement Guide

Jurisdiction: India (IT Act 2000, DPDPA 2023) & International (GDPR, CDA § 230) Entity: JJCoders Open Source Initiative Last Updated: 2026
Statutory Overview: JChatt operates strictly as an end-to-end encrypted protocol and neutral intermediary. Under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (India) and Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act (USA), JChatt and its maintainers are exempt from civil or criminal liability for communications transmitted by third parties. Because all payloads are encrypted client-side via AES-256-GCM before transmission, JChatt possesses no decryption keys and cannot inspect, filter, or log message contents.

1. Intermediary Status & Safe Harbor Immunity (Section 79, IT Act 2000)

In accordance with Section 2(1)(w) and Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, read with the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021:

  • Neutral Conduit: JChatt merely provides a cryptographic message routing substrate. The transmission of every communication is initiated entirely and solely by the end-user.
  • No Receiver Selection: JChatt does not choose, alter, or select the recipient of any transmission; routing is determined solely by client public keys.
  • No Content Modification: JChatt does not select, curate, screen, or modify the information contained in any transmission.
  • Absence of Technical Access: Due to mathematical end-to-end encryption, JChatt has zero technical knowledge of the contents of any message, audio packet, or file attachment.

2. Mandatory Grievance Redressal Mechanism (Rule 3(2), IT Rules 2021)

Under Rule 3(2) of the IT Intermediary Guidelines, JChatt has appointed a Resident Grievance Officer to address user complaints, illegal content reports, and law enforcement communications.

Resident Grievance Officer

3. Compliance with Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA)

India's DPDPA 2023 sets rigorous standards for Data Fiduciaries. JChatt complies through absolute architectural data minimization:

DPDPA Section Statutory Requirement JChatt Architecture Fulfillment
Section 5 & 6 Notice and Consent for processing personal data JChatt requires zero phone numbers, emails, or names. No personal data is requested or processed.
Section 8(1) Obligation to ensure data accuracy and security Zero centralized storage. Keys reside solely in user's device Keystore/IndexedDB with AES-256-GCM.
Section 8(7) Erasure upon purpose completion or consent withdrawal Clearing app data or deleting account locally wipes all cryptographic keys immediately and permanently.
Section 9 Processing of children's data Users must be 18+ (or have parental supervision). Zero behavioral tracking, zero profiling, zero targeted advertising.
Section 12-14 Right to access, correction, and grievance redressal Data principal rights are honored natively: user holds 100% of their data; grievance desk accessible via email.

4. Law Enforcement & Government Subpoena Guidelines

This section establishes our formal policy for judicial requests, subpoenas, and court orders issued under statutory authority:

Technical Boundary Notice for Law Enforcement: JChatt is architected with zero-knowledge cryptography. We cannot comply with any request to provide cleartext message contents, call audio, contacts, IP address history, or cryptographic private keys, because we do not possess them. No court order or warrant can compel the production of data that does not exist.
Category of Data Requested Technical Availability Our Legal Response
Message Contents (Cleartext) Technically Impossible All messages are encrypted client-side with AES-256-GCM. JChatt holds no keys.
Audio / Video Call Recordings Technically Impossible Calls are direct WebRTC P2P streams with DTLS-SRTP encryption; no audio is recorded on servers.
Phone Number or Email Records Non-Existent JChatt never requests, requires, or stores phone numbers or emails.
Contact Books / Address Books Non-Existent Zero address book scraping; user contacts remain purely local.
Public Cryptographic Identifier Available We can confirm whether a publicly known public handle exists on the relay mailbox.

5. Zero Tolerance Policy: CSAM, Terrorism & Illegal Harm

JChatt strictly prohibits the use of its platform for Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), non-consensual intimate imagery, terrorism facilitation, or incitement of violent harm. While JChatt cannot view end-to-end encrypted private communications, JChatt actively:

  • Cooperates with recognized statutory bodies in accordance with applicable laws to dismantle public abuse hubs.
  • Permanently bans reported public handles involved in unlawful distribution upon verified legal notice.
  • Encourages immediate reporting of illicit activity to local law enforcement and our Grievance Desk at grievance@jjcoders.org.

6. DMCA & Copyright Infringement Notice (17 U.S.C. § 512)

If you believe any content hosted on JChatt's public web domains infringes your copyright, submit a statutory DMCA Notice to our Designated Agent:

Designated DMCA Agent: JChatt Copyright & Legal Team
Email: dmca@jjcoders.org
Required Details: (1) Identification of copyrighted work; (2) Specific infringing URL; (3) Contact details; (4) Statement of good faith belief; (5) Electronic signature under penalty of perjury.

7. United States Safe Harbor (CDA Section 230)

Pursuant to 47 U.S.C. § 230(c)(1), JChatt, its founders, and operators shall not be treated as the publisher or speaker of any information provided by another information content provider. Users assume 100% legal responsibility for any material they transmit.
